forui.one_liner: Minimal, shadcn-inspired widget library built for touch-first Flutter apps.
forui.what_it_does: Forui gives you 50+ clean, neutral widgets (buttons, dialogs, calendars, sheets, forms) that look the same on every platform. A CLI generates themes and styling boilerplate, and controllers are also exposed as Flutter Hooks.
use_when: You want a branded app that doesn't look like Material or iOS
Your app is mobile or tablet first
avoid_when: You need native iOS or Android look and feel
You need a stable 1.0 API today
strengths: Tested against every Flutter change via Flutter's customer test registry
Theme builder and CLI save setup time
Plays well alongside Material and Cupertino widgets
weaknesses: Still pre-1.0, so minor versions can break your code
Smaller catalog than full kits like GetWidget
forui.setup_notes: Wrap your app in FTheme; no native setup.

alternatives.name: shadcn_ui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Closer to the default shadcn/ui style with a larger community

alternatives.name: shadcn_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: More components (84) and works without Material at all

shadcn_ui.one_liner: Port of shadcn/ui to Flutter with customizable, neutral components.
shadcn_ui.what_it_does: shadcn_ui brings shadcn/ui's default style to Flutter: forms, cards, dialogs, calendars, tables, popovers and inputs. Components are themed through ShadTheme and can sit inside a MaterialApp.
use_when: Your team already designs in shadcn/ui on the web
You want web, desktop and mobile to look identical
avoid_when: You need platform-native look on iOS
You want to own and edit the component code like shadcn on the web
strengths: Covers forms and data-entry components well
weaknesses: Ships as a dependency, not copy-in code
shadcn_ui.setup_notes: Use ShadApp or wrap in ShadTheme.

alternatives.name: forui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Touch-first, with a theme builder and hooks support

dio.one_liner: Full-featured HTTP client with interceptors, cancellation and file transfer.
dio.what_it_does: Dio sends HTTP requests with a configurable client: base URLs, headers, timeouts, interceptors for auth and logging, request cancellation, form data and upload/download progress.
use_when: You need interceptors for auth tokens or retries
You upload or download files with progress
You generate API clients with retrofit
avoid_when: You only make a few simple GET requests (package:http is lighter)
strengths: Works on every platform including web
weaknesses: Heavier API than package:http for simple cases
Web support has some adapter limits

alternatives.name: http
alternatives.why_pick_it: Smaller, official, enough for simple requests

alternatives.name: retrofit
alternatives.why_pick_it: Generates typed API clients on top of dio

flutter_bloc.one_liner: Widgets that connect BLoC and Cubit state to your Flutter UI.
flutter_bloc.what_it_does: flutter_bloc provides BlocProvider, BlocBuilder, BlocListener and friends, so widgets rebuild from state emitted by a Bloc or Cubit. Business logic stays out of widgets and is easy to unit test.
use_when: You want strict separation between UI and business logic
Your team values predictable, testable state changes
The app is medium to large
avoid_when: A small app where setState or signals would do
weaknesses: More boilerplate than Riverpod or signals
Event classes add ceremony for simple screens

alternatives.name: signals
alternatives.why_pick_it: Fine-grained reactivity with very little code

go_router.one_liner: Flutter team's URL-based router with deep links and nested navigation.
go_router.what_it_does: go_router maps URLs to screens with a declarative route table. It handles deep links, redirects (e.g. for auth), nested navigation with ShellRoute, and typed routes through an optional generator.
use_when: Your app needs deep links or web URLs
You want the router the Flutter team maintains
avoid_when: You expect a stable API between majors: it ships breaking majors often
weaknesses: Frequent major versions mean regular migrations
go_router.minimal_example: final router = GoRouter(routes: [GoRoute(path: '/', builder: (_, __) => const Home())]);

flutter_platform_widgets.one_liner: Single widgets that render Material on Android and Cupertino on iOS (discontinued).
flutter_platform_widgets.what_it_does: Provided PlatformXxx widgets that switched between Material and Cupertino implementations by platform. It was retired when Flutter split Material and Cupertino into separate packages.
use_when: Only to keep an existing app running while you migrate
weaknesses: Discontinued: no fixes or Flutter updates

alternatives.name: platform_adaptive_widgets
alternatives.why_pick_it: Its spiritual successor, built on material_ui and cupertino_ui
